heroHeadline: Senate Leaves for Memorial Day Recess Without Voting on $71.7B ICE/CBP Package — Trump's June 1 Deadline Missed; Vermont Prosecutor Refuses to Charge ICE Protesters in Escalating Standoff
heroSubtitle: On May 21–22, 2026, Senate Republicans departed Washington for the Memorial Day recess without holding a floor vote on the $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation package, missing President Trump's self-imposed June 1 signing deadline. Two provisions stalled the vote: a $1.776 billion DOJ 'anti-weaponization fund' to compensate Trump allies who allege political prosecution, and a $1 billion White House ballroom security line previously struck by the Senate Parliamentarian. The floor vote is now expected the week of June 1 when Congress returns. Separately, a Boston Globe investigation published May 22 reported that Chittenden County State's Attorney Sarah George has repeatedly declined to prosecute protesters arrested at an ICE surveillance center in South Burlington, Vermont — prompting a public feud with the governor and state police who have threatened to route future cases to the Vermont AG. ICE detention remains at a record 73,000+ with no oversight provisions in the stalled reconciliation package and the independent OIDO watchdog shut down as of May 5.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, Congressional records, Roll Call, CBS News, Boston Globe, and Vermont Public
